title: Note in Column Entry

illustrates.quote: Other transcriber’s notes follow the reference note(s). (See Sample 16-9: Note in Column Entry on page 16-27.)

blocks.text:
TABLE 7.1
Social Readjustment Rating Scale
(from Holmes and Rahe, 1967)
blocks.features: A ranked two-column table (Rank/Life event, Mean value), with a footnoted asterisk on the 'Marriage' row's mean value, explained in a note below the table.

notes.text: Marriage was arbitrarily assigned a stress value of 500; no event was found to be any more than twice as stressful. Here the values are reduced proportionally and range up to 100.

print.surroundingText: Cross-referenced from rule 16.8.1h, illustrating a transcriber's note ('Note(s) in the table below') placed before a table, followed by the reference note itself, followed by the table -- per rule 16.8.1's ordering (transcriber's note, blank line, reference note(s), then the table).
print.printFeatures: A shaded/bordered data table with a title above it and a small footnote below the table (marked by an asterisk keyed to row 7's value).

braille.notes: Line-number field width 5 (max line number 20, two digits, +3). Line 5 is the required transcriber's note ('Note to table entry.') inserted before the table per rule 16.8.1b; line 7 is the reference note itself (about the arbitrary stress value of 500), placed after a blank line and before the table proper (lines 10 onward), matching the ordering in rule 16.8.1c-d. Table rows use 1-3-style columns with braille row-leader dot-fill ('...') between the life-event label and its value.

resolution: illustrates.rule set to 16.8.1.h per standards-map.md's own BANA §16/B004 §11 worked-examples table (the project's established canonical id), not either run's own guess. print.blocks/print.notes follow Run B's schema ([ref:MARK] tokens inline + a separate print.notes[] array of {ref, placement, text}), matching this task's required schema; Run A instead folded each note's real content directly into a sibling print.blocks entry with no [ref:MARK] markers and always an empty print.notes[] -- a schema-level difference, not a content disagreement. braille.width: verified directly: line 13143 (the table's own header row, field width 5, digits(20)+3) is exactly 40 characters; the title line (13133, 41 characters) and the footnoted 'Marriage' row (13151, 41 characters) are one cell over, a genuine source anomaly on those two lines only, not grounds to null the whole item's width. braille.lines: the two runs' transcriptions disagreed on leading blank-cell counts / an inserted anomalous token on specific lines; resolved by direct re-extraction from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (U+2800 cells converted to spaces, fixed padding measured exactly) -- see differences.md for the line-by-line count.
